category: PCB interactive routing: modes, options & in-command shortcuts
description: The behaviours and keystrokes available while Route > Interactive Routing (and the differential-pair, multi-trace and tuning variants) is active: conflict-resolution modes, corner styles, look-ahead, width/via sources, layer changes, glossing, plus the general PCB editor shortcuts most used during layout.

tools.name: Routing Conflict Resolution modes (Ignore Obstacles / Walkaround / Push / Hug and Push / Stop At First Obstacle / AutoRoute)
tools.description: How the interactive router reacts to existing objects: Ignore Obstacles (route through, violations shown), Walkaround Obstacles, Push Obstacles (move other tracks/vias aside), Hug And Push Obstacles (follow contours then push), Stop At First Obstacle, plus AutoRoute Current Layer and AutoRoute Multilayer (route to the target automatically). The set enabled for cycling is chosen in PCB Editor > Interactive Routing; Shift+R cycles through the enabled ones while routing and the current mode is shown in the status bar/heads-up display.
tools.usage: Route > Interactive Routing, then Shift+R (cycle) or Tab > Properties panel > Interactive Routing Conflict Resolution

parameters.name: Current Mode
parameters.description: Active conflict-resolution mode.

parameters.name: Enabled modes
parameters.description: Preferences > PCB Editor > Interactive Routing > Routing Conflict Resolution checkboxes.

tools.example: Start in Walkaround for the first traces of a BGA escape, press Shift+R to switch to Push Obstacles when squeezing through a channel, then Shift+R again to return.
tools.notes: Push mode moves other objects and can create new violations elsewhere; watch the DRC overlay. AutoRoute modes are single-connection ActiveRoute-style helpers, not the Situs router.

tools.name: Shift+R (cycle conflict resolution mode)
tools.description: While interactively routing, cycles through the routing conflict resolution modes that are enabled in Preferences (Ignore, Walkaround, Push, Hug and Push, Stop at first obstacle, AutoRoute current layer, AutoRoute multilayer).
tools.usage: Shift+R (during Interactive Routing)
tools.example: Route > Interactive Routing, click the start pad, press Shift+R until the heads-up display reads 'Push Obstacles'.
tools.notes: Only modes ticked in PCB Editor > Interactive Routing are visited.

tools.name: Shift+Space (cycle corner mode) and Space (corner direction)
tools.description: Shift+Space cycles the five track corner modes: 45 Degree, 45 Degree with Arc, 90 Degree, 90 Degree with Arc and Any Angle. Space toggles the corner direction sub-mode (which segment bends first) within the current mode. Arc radius in the arc modes is adjusted with , and . (1 mil steps) or Shift+, / Shift+. (10 mil steps).
tools.usage: Shift+Space / Space (during Interactive Routing); , . Shift+, Shift+. for arc radius
tools.example: Press Shift+Space until '45 Degree with Arc' is shown, then press . several times to enlarge the mitre arc before committing the corner.
tools.notes: The corner mode is remembered for the next routing session; Any Angle is needed for teardrop-free RF bends.

tools.name: Look-Ahead segment (1)
tools.description: Toggles Look-Ahead placement mode: with it on, the hollow segment beyond the cursor previews the next segment so clicks commit only the solid segment, letting the router pre-plan corners. Off, every segment up to the cursor is committed on click.
tools.usage: 1 (during Interactive Routing) - toggle Look-Ahead on/off
tools.example: With Look-Ahead on, aim the hollow segment down the channel, click to commit the solid segment, repeat.
tools.notes: Many users prefer Look-Ahead off for BGA breakouts; the setting persists in the Properties panel while routing.

tools.name: Automatic loop removal (Shift+D)
tools.description: Toggles Automatically Remove Loops: when a new route returns to the same net, the redundant old loop is deleted, which is how tracks are re-routed by simply routing a new path over the old one. Shift+D toggles it during routing; the default is set in PCB Editor > Interactive Routing.
tools.usage: Shift+D (during Interactive Routing); Preferences > PCB Editor > Interactive Routing > Automatically Remove Loops
tools.example: Route a fresh path from pad A to pad B over an existing connection: the old segments disappear as soon as the loop closes.
tools.notes: Disable loop removal for nets that intentionally form loops (e.g. guard rings, power meshes); a per-net Remove Loops option also exists in the net's Properties.

tools.name: Track width source (3) and Shift+W favourite widths
tools.description: 3 cycles the routing width source between User Choice, Rule Minimum, Rule Preferred and Rule Maximum of the applicable Width rule; Shift+W opens the Choose Width dialog listing the favourite widths defined in PCB Editor > Interactive Routing. Tab opens the Properties panel to type an explicit width.
tools.usage: 3 / Shift+W / Tab (during Interactive Routing)

parameters.name: Track Width Mode
parameters.description: User Choice | Rule Minimum | Rule Preferred | Rule Maximum.

parameters.name: Favorite Interactive Routing Widths
parameters.description: Preference table of quick widths (imperial/metric).

tools.example: Press 3 until 'Rule Minimum' is shown to neck down through a BGA field, then 3 again to return to Rule Preferred outside it.
tools.notes: A user width outside the rule Min/Max is clipped to the rule limits unless the rule is disabled.

tools.name: Via size source (4) and Shift+V favourite vias
tools.description: 4 cycles the via size source (User Choice, Rule Minimum, Rule Preferred, Rule Maximum of the Routing Via Style rule); Shift+V opens the Choose Via Size dialog with the favourite via sizes/templates from PCB Editor > Interactive Routing. 6 cycles the Via Type (layer span) when changing layers; 8 pops up the Via Type list.
tools.usage: 4 / Shift+V / 6 / 8 (during Interactive Routing)

parameters.name: Via Size Mode
parameters.description: User Choice | Rule Minimum | Rule Preferred | Rule Maximum.

parameters.name: Via Type
parameters.description: One of the via spans defined in Layer Stack Manager > Via Types.

tools.example: During a layer change press 8 and pick 'uVia Top-L2' from the list, then continue routing on Mid Layer 1.
tools.notes: In Template preferred mode the Routing Via Style rule limits the choices to enabled templates.

tools.name: Layer change while routing (numeric * + - , Ctrl+Shift+Wheel, Ctrl+L, 1-9)
tools.description: Numeric keypad * or + switches to the next enabled signal layer (dropping a via), - to the previous; Shift+* goes to the previous signal layer; Ctrl+Shift+Mouse Wheel cycles enabled signal layers; Ctrl+L pops up the list of routing layers; numeric keypad 1-9 jumps directly to the n-th signal layer. Layers not permitted by the Routing Layers rule are skipped.
tools.usage: * | + | - | Shift+* | Ctrl+Shift+Wheel | Ctrl+L | numeric 1..9 (during Interactive Routing)
tools.example: Route on Top, press * to drop a via and continue on Mid Layer 1, press Ctrl+L and choose Bottom Layer to finish.
tools.notes: Outside routing, + and - simply change the current layer; * moves between signal layers only.

tools.name: 2 (add via without layer change) and / (fanout via)
tools.description: 2 inserts a via at the cursor and keeps routing on the same layer (useful for via-in-line stitching or test vias); / places a fanout via and immediately waits for the next fanout, the fast way to escape rows of SMD pads.
tools.usage: 2 | / (during Interactive Routing)
tools.example: Click an SMD pad, press / to drop the fanout via next to it, click the next pad, press / again.
tools.notes: Fanout vias follow the Fanout Control and Routing Via Style rules.

tools.name: L (switch layer of the connection at a multilayer pad)
tools.description: While starting a route from a through-hole pad or via, L flips the connection to the next signal layer without adding a via. Outside a routing command L opens the View Configuration panel (Layers & Colors), and while a component is being moved L flips it to the other side of the board.
tools.usage: L (during Interactive Routing from a multilayer pad); L (idle) opens View Configuration; L while dragging a component flips it to the other side
tools.example: Start routing from J1 pin 3 on Top, press L to begin the same connection on Bottom Layer instead.
tools.notes: Ctrl+L lists routing layers; Shift+S toggles Single Layer Mode for clarity.

tools.name: Ctrl+Click (Auto-Complete) and 9 (swap ends)
tools.description: Ctrl+Click while routing asks the router to auto-complete the remaining segments to the target pad using the current conflict mode; 9 jumps the cursor/route start to the opposite end of the current connection so you can route from the other pad; 7 cycles through the connections of a pad that has several.
tools.usage: Ctrl+Click | 9 | 7 (during Interactive Routing)
tools.example: Route two segments out of a BGA, then Ctrl+Click to let the router finish the rest of the connection to the capacitor.
tools.notes: Auto-complete respects Routing Layers and clearance rules but not length tuning.

tools.name: Backspace / Esc / Enter (unwind, terminate, commit)
tools.description: Backspace unwinds the last committed segment (repeat to back out further), Esc terminates the current route keeping everything already committed, Enter (or click) commits the segments up to the cursor. Right-click also terminates.
tools.usage: Backspace | Esc | Enter (during Interactive Routing)
tools.example: Committed a corner too early: press Backspace once, re-aim, click to commit again.
tools.notes: Ctrl+Z after routing undoes the whole route as one transaction.

tools.name: Glossing controls (Shift+Ctrl+G, Ctrl+Shift hold, Route > Gloss Selected)
tools.description: Glossing smooths committed routing (removing kinks, tightening corners, pulling tracks away from pads). Shift+Ctrl+G cycles the Gloss Effort (Routed) between Off, Weak and Strong while routing; holding Ctrl+Shift temporarily inhibits automatic glossing; Route > Gloss Selected / Retrace Selected apply glossing or re-width/re-gap to selected copper afterwards. Parameters live in PCB Editor > Gloss And Retrace.
tools.usage: Shift+Ctrl+G | hold Ctrl+Shift (during routing); Route > Gloss Selected; Preferences > PCB Editor > Gloss And Retrace

parameters.name: Gloss Effort (Routed)
parameters.description: Off | Weak | Strong.

parameters.name: Gloss Effort (Neighbor)
parameters.description: How much neighbouring tracks are glossed when pushed.

tools.example: Set Gloss Effort Strong for general routing; hold Ctrl+Shift while dropping a track in a tight serpentine to stop the router from straightening it.
tools.notes: Strong glossing may alter tuned lengths; keep Weak/Off in length-matched areas.

tools.name: Differential pair routing keys (Shift+B, Shift+6, B, C, 5)
tools.description: During Interactive Differential Pair Routing / Multi-Routing: Shift+B cycles the Width-Gap pairings (Rule Minimum/Preferred/Maximum) of the Differential Pairs Routing rule or increases spacing between multi-routed traces; B decreases multi-trace spacing; C sets multi-trace spacing to the Track-Track clearance; Shift+6 cycles the Gap value alone; 5 cycles via patterns for the pair's layer change.
tools.usage: Shift+B | Shift+6 | B | C | 5 (during diff-pair or multi-trace routing)
tools.example: Route a USB pair: press Shift+B to select Rule Preferred width/gap, press 5 during the via drop to choose a staggered via pattern.
tools.notes: Changing width or gap independently with 3 / Shift+6 can break the pair's coupling rule; DRC will flag it.

tools.name: Subnet swapping (Shift+C / Shift+T)
tools.description: Shift+C enables subnet (pin) swapping during routing so the router may retarget the connection to an equivalent pin/subnet; Shift+T cycles through the available swappable target subnets. Requires pin/part swapping to be enabled on the components (Tools > Pin/Part Swapping).
tools.usage: Shift+C | Shift+T (during Interactive Routing)
tools.example: Routing FPGA I/O: press Shift+C, then Shift+T until the ratsnest points at the nearest swappable pin, and route to it; push the swap back with Design > Update Schematics.
tools.notes: Swaps are recorded and must be back-annotated to the schematic.

tools.name: Length tuning gauge (Shift+G) and tuning patterns
tools.description: Shift+G toggles the on-screen length tuning gauge that shows current length against the Length/Matched Lengths targets during Interactive Length Tuning and diff-pair tuning. In the tuning command, Tab opens the Properties panel to choose the pattern (Mitered Lines, Mitered Arcs, Rounded), amplitude, gap, target source (Manual, From Rules, From Net/xSignal), and the keys , . / Shift adjust amplitude/space on the fly.
tools.usage: Route > Interactive Length Tuning, then Shift+G; Tab for Properties; , . to change amplitude; 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 keys change pattern parameters as shown in the heads-up

parameters.name: Target Length
parameters.description: Manual, From Rules or From Net/xSignal.

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Mitered Lines | Mitered Arcs | Rounded (accordion/trombone/sawtooth results).

tools.example: Set Matched Lengths rule on the xSignal class, start Interactive Length Tuning on the shortest net, press Shift+G, drag along the track until the gauge turns green.
tools.notes: Tuning segments are ordinary tracks/arcs afterwards; glossing can undo them.

tools.name: Ctrl+W (clearance boundaries) and Shift+F (Follow mode)
tools.description: Ctrl+W toggles display of the clearance boundary halo around obstacles while routing, showing exactly how close the track can get; Shift+F toggles Follow mode, where the new route hugs a selected existing track/arc path at the rule clearance.
tools.usage: Ctrl+W | Shift+F (during Interactive Routing)
tools.example: Select a reference track, start routing the neighbouring net, press Shift+F so the new trace follows the reference around the bend.
tools.notes: Shift+F outside routing opens Find Similar Objects.

tools.name: Tab (Properties panel during a command)
tools.description: While placing or routing, Tab pauses the command and opens the Properties panel for the object being placed (track width, via size, layer, net, corner mode, conflict resolution, teardrop and tuning options), so settings can be changed on the fly and remembered for subsequent objects of that type.
tools.usage: Tab (during any placement/routing command); Esc or click returns to the command
tools.example: Place > Via, press Tab, set Diameter 0.5 mm / Hole 0.25 mm / Net GND, click the board to place several identical vias.
tools.notes: Defaults for objects when no command is running are set in Preferences > PCB Editor > Defaults.

tools.name: Shift+S (Single Layer Mode)
tools.description: Toggles Single Layer Mode, which hides, greys or monochromes all layers except the current one (behaviour chosen in PCB Editor > Board Insight Display: Hide Other Layers / Gray Scale Other Layers / Monochrome Other Layers). Invaluable when routing dense inner layers.
tools.usage: Shift+S (PCB editor); View Configuration panel > View Options > Single Layer Mode
tools.example: Press Shift+S, then + / - to step through layers one at a time while inspecting a plane split.
tools.notes: Combined with the L shortcut (View Configuration) and Layer Sets for quick layer views.

tools.name: Q (toggle units) and Ctrl+M (measure distance)
tools.description: Q switches the document between metric (mm) and imperial (mil) units immediately, affecting grids, dialogs and the heads-up display; Ctrl+M starts Reports > Measure Distance for a two-click point-to-point measurement showing total, X and Y distances.
tools.usage: Q | Ctrl+M (PCB editor)
tools.example: Press Q to see mils, Ctrl+M and click two pad centres to read the pitch, Shift+C to clear the measurement graphics.
tools.notes: Reports > Measure Primitives / Measure Selected Objects measure edge-to-edge and selected copper length.

tools.name: G / Ctrl+G / Ctrl+E (grids and snap)
tools.description: G pops up the Snap Grid menu (preset grids, Set Global Snap Grid, Grid Manager); Ctrl+G opens the grid editor for the grid under the cursor (Cartesian or polar); Ctrl+E opens the Snap Options pop-up to choose which object hotspots (pads, vias, track ends, guides) are used for Objects Snap. Axis and object snapping are also configured under Design > Board Options.
tools.usage: G | Ctrl+G | Ctrl+E (PCB editor)
tools.example: Press G and choose 0.05 mm, then Ctrl+E and enable only 'Object Hotspot Snap' for pads while routing to pad centres.
tools.notes: Grid Manager (Design > Board Options > Grids) defines multiple local grids with priorities.

tools.name: Shift+H / Shift+M (Heads Up Display and Board Insight Lens)
tools.description: Shift+H toggles the Board Insight Heads Up Display (cursor coordinates, current layer, net, routing status); Shift+M toggles the Board Insight Lens, a movable magnifier that can show a different layer set or single-layer view. Options for both live in PCB Editor > Board Insight Modes / Board Insight Lens.
tools.usage: Shift+H | Shift+M (PCB editor)
tools.example: Press Shift+M, hover over a BGA to inspect escape routing at 4x while the main view stays zoomed out.
tools.notes: Lens magnification, size and layer mode are set in Preferences > PCB Editor > Board Insight Lens; the lens can follow the cursor or be pinned in place.

tools.name: View > Fit commands (Fit Board, Fit Document, Area, Selected Objects, Filtered Objects, Around Point)
tools.description: Zoom commands of the PCB editor: Fit Document (Ctrl+PgDn) shows every object, Fit Board frames the board shape, Area (drag a rectangle), Selected Objects, Filtered Objects, Around Point, Zoom In/Out (PgUp/PgDn), Previous zoom, plus Refresh (End) and Flip Board (View > Flip Board, Ctrl+F) to view from the bottom.
tools.usage: View > Fit Board | Fit Document | Area | Selected Objects | Filtered Objects | Around Point | Zoom In | Zoom Out | Refresh | Flip Board
tools.example: Select a net in the PCB panel, View > Selected Objects (or the panel's Zoom option) to frame it.
tools.notes: Mouse: wheel pans, Ctrl+wheel zooms, right-drag pans, Shift+wheel pans horizontally (configurable in Mouse Wheel Configuration).

tools.name: Edit > Select submenu (PCB)
tools.description: Selection commands for the PCB editor: Inside Area, Outside Area, Touching Line, Touching Rectangle, Lasso Select, All, Board, Net (S N), Physical Connection (S P), Physical Connection Single Layer, Component Connections, Component Nets, Room Connections, All on Layer (S Y), Free Objects, All Locked, Off Grid Pads, Toggle Selection, Connected Copper (Ctrl+H), plus Select Similar via Find Similar Objects. Deselect has the matching set.
tools.usage: Edit > Select > ... ; shortcuts: S A (all), S N (net), S P (physical connection), S Y (all on layer), Ctrl+H (connected copper)
tools.example: Edit > Select > Physical Connection, click a track: the whole routed path between pads is selected for deletion or width change.
tools.notes: Selection Filter (Properties panel) restricts what these commands pick up.

tools.name: Edit > Jump submenu (PCB)
tools.description: Moves the cursor (and view) to a location: Absolute Origin, Current Origin, New Location (typed X/Y), Component (by designator), Net, Pad, String, Error Marker, Selection, and Location Marks 1-0 set with Edit > Set Location Marks. Jump to Error Marker steps through DRC violations.
tools.usage: Edit > Jump > Absolute Origin | Current Origin | New Location | Component | Net | Pad | String | Error Marker | Selection | Location Mark

parameters.name: Designator / Net / Pad / String
parameters.description: Target identifier typed in the prompt.

tools.example: Edit > Jump > Component, type U7 - the view centres on U7 with the cursor on its reference point.
tools.notes: Verify letter shortcuts in your build via the menu accelerators; the Navigator and PCB panels offer the same jumps with zoom.

tools.name: Move / drag keys (Space, X, Y, L, Ctrl while dragging, Shift+wheel)
tools.description: While moving or placing an object: Space rotates by the Rotation Step (Shift+Space rotates the other way), X and Y mirror about the axes (components only during placement), L flips a component to the other side, holding Ctrl while dragging a track drags it with its connected segments (Drag) versus Move, and Ctrl+drag on a component keeps connectivity. The rotation step and Ctrl/drag behaviour are set in PCB Editor > General and > Interactive Routing (Component Dragging).
tools.usage: Space | Shift+Space | X | Y | L | Ctrl (during move/place)

parameters.name: Rotation Step
parameters.description: Preferences > PCB Editor > General > Rotation Step (default 90).

parameters.name: Component push/avoid
parameters.description: PCB Editor > Interactive Routing > Component Dragging: none, push obstacles, avoid obstacles.

tools.example: Click-hold a resistor, press Space twice to rotate 180 degrees, press L to move it to the bottom side, release.
tools.notes: Edit > Move > Move Selection by X,Y gives numeric offsets; Rotate Selection prompts for an angle.

tools.name: Shift+C / X A / Ctrl+PgDn (clear filter, clear selection, fit)
tools.description: Shift+C clears the current filter/mask and measurement graphics (PCB Filter, Find Similar, measurement results); Edit > Deselect > All (X A) clears the selection; Ctrl+PgDn fits the whole document in view.
tools.usage: Shift+C | X A | Ctrl+PgDn (PCB editor)
tools.example: After a PCB Filter mask press Shift+C to restore full visibility, then Ctrl+PgDn to see the whole board.
tools.notes: Clear button in the PCB Filter panel does the same as Shift+C.

tools.name: PCB Editor > Interactive Routing preferences
tools.description: Preference page defining routing defaults: enabled Routing Conflict Resolution modes and the current mode; Interactive Routing Options (Automatically Terminate Routing, Automatically Remove Loops, Remove Loops With Vias, Restrict To 90/45, Follow Mouse Trail, Display Clearance Boundaries, Reduce Clearance Display Area); Dragging (Preserve Angle When Dragging, Ignore Obstacles/Avoid Obstacles/Push Obstacles, Component pushing, Unselected via/track behaviour); Interactive Routing Width/Via Size Sources (Pickup Track Width From Existing Routes, Track Width Mode, Via Size Mode); Favorite Interactive Routing Widths table.
tools.usage: Preferences > PCB Editor > Interactive Routing

parameters.name: Routing Conflict Resolution
parameters.description: Enabled modes and the default mode.

parameters.name: Track Width Mode / Via Size Mode
parameters.description: User Choice | Rule Minimum | Rule Preferred | Rule Maximum.

parameters.name: Favorite Interactive Routing Widths
parameters.description: List offered by Shift+W.

tools.example: Enable Walkaround, Push and Hug And Push; set Track Width Mode = Rule Preferred; add 0.15, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5 mm as favourites.
tools.notes: Gloss/retrace strengths are on the separate Gloss And Retrace page.

tools.name: Route > Retrace Selected / Re-route (Route > Interactive Routing over existing)
tools.description: Retrace Selected re-applies the current Width and Differential Pairs Routing rules to selected routing (re-widths and re-gaps without changing the path), governed by PCB Editor > Gloss And Retrace parameters. Re-routing a path is done by routing a new connection over the old one with Automatically Remove Loops enabled, or by dragging a segment (Drag mode) so connected segments follow.
tools.usage: Route > Retrace Selected; Route > Interactive Routing (with loop removal) to re-route
tools.example: Change the DDR Width rule to 0.11 mm, select the DDR tracks (PCB Filter InNetClass('DDR') And IsTrack), Route > Retrace Selected.
tools.notes: Retrace never changes layers or vias; use Un-Route + re-route for topology changes.

tools.name: Interactive Routing Properties (routing-time Properties panel fields)
tools.description: The Properties panel shown by Tab during Interactive Routing exposes: Net, Layer, Width (with source mode), Via diameter/hole/type, Corner Style and Setback/Arc radius, Routing Conflict Resolution, Interactive Routing Options (Look Ahead, Automatically Terminate, Remove Loops, Follow Mouse Trail, Restrict to 90/45), Routing Width Constraints (Min/Preferred/Max from rule), Via Constraints, Glossing Effort (Routed/Neighbor) and Teardrops/Length tuning toggles where applicable.
tools.usage: Route > Interactive Routing > Tab

parameters.name: Width / Via
parameters.description: Current values and rule limits.

parameters.name: Interactive Routing Options
parameters.description: Per-session behaviour toggles.

tools.example: Press Tab, set Corner Style to Rounded with Setback 0.5 mm, Gloss Effort Weak, then continue routing RF traces.
tools.notes: Values set here persist until the next Interactive Routing session changes them.

tools.name: Route Guide (ActiveRoute guided routing)
tools.description: In the ActiveRoute panel, Route Guide lets you draw a corridor (polyline with width) that the ActiveRoute engine follows for the selected connections, controlling path, layer usage and track spacing/ordering before pressing ActiveRoute. Guides are removed after routing or cleared explicitly.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB ActiveRoute > Route Guide; select connections, draw guide, click ActiveRoute

parameters.name: Guide width
parameters.description: Corridor width that limits spreading.

parameters.name: Track-Track Space
parameters.description: Spacing used inside the corridor.

tools.example: Select 8 DDR data connections, click Route Guide, draw the corridor between two BGA fields, set Track-Track Space to clearance, click ActiveRoute.
tools.notes: Works with Layers, Meander (tuning) and Pin Swap options in the same panel.
